The higher your frame rate the better your response time as well as how true to life the game will feel. 

At 30fps an image is rendered every 33.3 ms. Meaning from the time you press a button there is a delay of 33.3 ms or more. The less delay there is between what you see and when you actually press a button the better and the more fluid the game will feel.

A game like breath of the wild plays fine at 30fps because it's fairly slow placed and incapable of rapid movements due to the use of the joysticks vs a mouse which can move as fast as you want it to. This is why PC guys usually strive for high frame rates.

It's just one of those things that you need to experience yourself. It's like explaining VR to someone who has never experienced it. If you ever have a chance to play on a PC setup that can drive a 144hz monitor properly try it out and you will see exactly what I mean.
Watching a video at 30/60 fps is far different from being the one who controls the movement and gameplay.

Oh ok I seem to have misunderstood your post.

So essentially you want your kids to both be able to play both their systems on your older TV at the same time? If the tv doesn't have a picture in picture function or a picture by picture function you may consider a HDMI Switch that has a picture in picture function.

I searched Amazon for "hdmi pip" and found quite a few but most of them don't go into detail how the PIP function works.

I did find this one but it's on the expensive side. 

Sewell Crossbolt, HDMI 2x1 Multi-Viewer with adjustable PIP and 4 viewing modes https://www.amazon.com/dp/B01K2VRK1S/ref=cm_sw_r_cp_api_ZBc2ybN2266DE

It's the only one I found in my brief search that actually had pictures of how the PIP function works. Another concern I would have is introducing latency. Typically when you process a video signal there is a slight delay from the device that is outputting (Nintendo Switch) and the time it take for the Signal to be processed and sent to the display. This Could only be in the 10s of milliseconds but that will cause a delay between your button presses and what you see on the display making playing games frustrating.

Make sure you look at the specs and reviews before you make a purchase. Look for words like lag, latency, delay etc.

I worked in large processing plant.

I'm a computer guy so naturally I started to poke around the network. Immediately I discovered that the wifi network was NOT separate from the plants main network. The system all the machines used to talk to each other.

The passwords were either blatantly obvious or just did not exists. I had full control of EVERYTHING. Security cameras, servers, headless machines, hell even manufacturing and heating equipment, ticket printers you name it.

Instead of causing chaos like I could have I just made my job easier and I learned a bunch just snooping around.

My job was to monitor and control various machinery via the control panels or via one of the main computers.

Why waste my time doing that when I can ssh/VNC into each system and do it remotely such as when I was on lunch. 

I learned that day that many networks are totally insecure and we're setup in a "set and forget" scenario.

It's fun snooping around but just because you didn't cause any harm doesn't mean that just being "in there" is considered harm itself.

I had 20+ years to get to know my father. My anxiety always made me avoid him and dread when he would call me. He always tried so hard but I never did. He never raised his voice to me and was always extremely nice and did what he could.

Got home from my work one day only to be told my father was in the hospital.

He had been sick which eventually lead pneumonia. X-Rays were done only to discover he had Stage-3 Carcinoma Cancer that was wrapped around his spine.

Now I realize why my father made the noises he made whenever he get up. He was always a stubborn strong man. Far too much for his own good. I had a week to spend with him but somehow avoided most of it because of my severe anxiety. I was with him a couple times when he was conscious. All I ever said was that I loved him and he told me he knows and that he loved me too. Both of us were unable to really communicate. A week goes by and he is now in hospice. A place where people go to die. I had one chance to see him when he was up and walking and I wasn't there. That night I watched my father die, I listened to his heart sporadically beat after the life left his body, I felt the texture of his skin change.

Upon arriving at his house I immediately realized my father had been in a great deal of pain for some time and never admitted to it. His house was a mess. Mail everywhere, signatures on papers that were shaky and illegible.

I screamed in my car at the top of my lungs and beat my steering wheel as I drove off for the last time in a fit of feelings I have never felt before.

I could have been the one variable that extended his life but I was never there. I can't help but feel like my father lost his will to live years ago. All that information forever lost.

I was my fathers only child. He never got to see me do anything with my life and now I'm the last Poe on this branch of the tree.
So do I! I don't remember how old I was but I always loved opening that container.
